title: Rigveda 6.51: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 6.51: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 6.51 is a hymn of 16 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 6, the family book of Bharadvāja. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 468v-470v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 6.51.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 8, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 468v
translation.original_text:
1ud u̱ tyac cakṣu̱r mahi̍ mi̱trayo̱r ām̐ eti̍ pri̱yaṁ varu̍ṇayo̱r ada̍bdham | ṛ̱tasya̱ śuci̍ darśa̱tam anī̍kaṁ ru̱kmo na di̱va udi̍tā̱ vy a̍dyaut ||
2veda̱ yas trīṇi̍ vi̱dathā̍ny eṣāṁ de̱vānā̱ṁ janma̍ sanu̱tar ā ca̱ vipra̍ḥ | ṛ̱ju marte̍ṣu vṛji̱nā ca̱ paśya̍nn a̱bhi ca̍ṣṭe̱ sūro̍ a̱rya evā̍n ||
translation.text:
1THAT mighty eye of Varuṇa and Mitra, infallible and dear, is moving upward. The pure and lovely face of holy Order hath shone like gold of heaven in its arising.
2The Sage who knows these Gods' three ranks and orders, and all their generations near and distant, Beholding good and evil acts of mortals, Sûra marks well the doing of the pious.

translation.original_ref: RV 6.51.3-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 8, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 469r
translation.original_text:
3stu̱ṣa u̍ vo ma̱ha ṛ̱tasya̍ go̱pān adi̍tim mi̱traṁ varu̍ṇaṁ sujā̱tān | a̱rya̱maṇa̱m bhaga̱m ada̍bdhadhītī̱n acchā̍ voce sadha̱nya̍ḥ pāva̱kān ||
4ri̱śāda̍sa̱ḥ satpa̍tī̱m̐r ada̍bdhān ma̱ho rājña̍ḥ suvasa̱nasya̍ dā̱tṝn | yūna̍ḥ sukṣa̱trān kṣaya̍to di̱vo nṝn ā̍di̱tyān yā̱my adi̍tiṁ duvo̱yu ||
5dyau̱3̱̍ṣ pita̱ḥ pṛthi̍vi̱ māta̱r adhru̱g agne̍ bhrātar vasavo mṛ̱ḻatā̍ naḥ | viśva̍ ādityā adite sa̱joṣā̍ a̱smabhya̱ṁ śarma̍ bahu̱laṁ vi ya̍nta ||
translation.text:
3I praise you Guards of mighty Law eternal, Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa, the noble, Aryaman, Bhaga, all whose thoughts are faithful: hither I call the Bright who share in common.
4Lords of the brave, infallible, foe-destroyers, great Kings, bestowers of fair homes to dwell in, Young, Heroes, ruling heaven with strong dominion, Âdityas, Aditi I seek with worship.
5O Heaven our Father, Earth our guileless Mother, O Brother Agni, and ye Vasus, bless us. Grant us, O Aditi and ye Âdityas, all of one mind, your manifold protection.

translation.original_ref: RV 6.51.6-8 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 8, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 469v
translation.original_text:
6mā no̱ vṛkā̍ya vṛ̱kye̍ samasmā aghāya̱te rī̍radhatā yajatrāḥ | yū̱yaṁ hi ṣṭhā ra̱thyo̍ nas ta̱nūnā̍ṁ yū̱yaṁ dakṣa̍sya̱ vaca̍so babhū̱va ||
7mā va̱ eno̍ a̱nyakṛ̍tam bhujema̱ mā tat ka̍rma vasavo̱ yac caya̍dhve | viśva̍sya̱ hi kṣaya̍tha viśvadevāḥ sva̱yaṁ ri̱pus ta̱nva̍ṁ rīriṣīṣṭa ||
8nama̱ id u̱graṁ nama̱ ā vi̍vāse̱ namo̍ dādhāra pṛthi̱vīm u̱ta dyām | namo̍ de̱vebhyo̱ nama̍ īśa eṣāṁ kṛ̱taṁ ci̱d eno̱ nama̱sā vi̍vāse ||
translation.text:
6Give us not up to any evil creature, as spoil to wolf or she-wolf, O ye Holy. For ye are they who guide aright our bodies, ye are the rulers of our speech and vigour.
7Let us not suffer for the sin of others, nor do the deed which ye, O Vasus, punish. Ye, Universal Gods! are all-controllers: may he do harm unto himself who hates Me.
8Mighty is homage: I adopt and use it. Homage hath held in place the earth and heaven. Homage to Gods! Homage commands and rules them. I banish even committed sin by homage

translation.original_ref: RV 6.51.9-11 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 8, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 470r
translation.original_text:
9ṛ̱tasya̍ vo ra̱thya̍ḥ pū̱tada̍kṣān ṛ̱tasya̍ pastya̱sado̱ ada̍bdhān | tām̐ ā namo̍bhir uru̱cakṣa̍so̱ nṝn viśvā̍n va̱ ā na̍me ma̱ho ya̍jatrāḥ ||
10te hi śreṣṭha̍varcasa̱s ta u̍ nas ti̱ro viśvā̍ni duri̱tā naya̍nti | su̱kṣa̱trāso̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̱gnir ṛ̱tadhī̍tayo vakma̱rāja̍satyāḥ ||
11te na̱ indra̍ḥ pṛthi̱vī kṣāma̍ vardhan pū̱ṣā bhago̱ adi̍ti̱ḥ pañca̱ janā̍ḥ | su̱śarmā̍ṇa̱ḥ svava̍saḥ sunī̱thā bhava̍ntu naḥ sutrā̱trāsa̍ḥ sugo̱pāḥ ||
translation.text:
9You Furtherers of Law, pure in your spirit, infallible, dwellers in the home of Order, To you all Heroes mighty and far-seeing I bow me down, O Holy Ones, with homage.
10For these are they who shine with noblest splendour; through all our troubles these conduct us safely- Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, mighty Rulers, trueminded, faithful to the hymn's controllers.
11May they, Earth, Aditi, Indra, Bhaga, Pûshan increase our laud, increase the Fivefold people. Giving good help, good refuge, goodly guidance, be they our good deliverers, good protectors.

translation.original_ref: RV 6.51.12-16 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 8, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 470v
translation.original_text:
12nū sa̱dmāna̍ṁ di̱vyaṁ naṁśi̍ devā̱ bhāra̍dvājaḥ suma̱tiṁ yā̍ti̱ hotā̍ | ā̱sā̱nebhi̱r yaja̍māno mi̱yedhai̍r de̱vānā̱ṁ janma̍ vasū̱yur va̍vanda ||
13apa̱ tyaṁ vṛ̍ji̱naṁ ri̱puṁ ste̱nam a̍gne durā̱dhya̍m | da̱vi̱ṣṭham a̍sya satpate kṛ̱dhī su̱gam ||
14grāvā̍ṇaḥ soma no̱ hi ka̍ṁ sakhitva̱nāya̍ vāva̱śuḥ | ja̱hī ny a1̱̍triṇa̍m pa̱ṇiṁ vṛko̱ hi ṣaḥ ||
15yū̱yaṁ hi ṣṭhā su̍dānava̱ indra̍jyeṣṭhā a̱bhidya̍vaḥ | kartā̍ no̱ adhva̱nn ā su̱gaṁ go̱pā a̱mā ||
16api̱ panthā̍m aganmahi svasti̱gām a̍ne̱hasa̍m | yena̱ viśvā̱ḥ pari̱ dviṣo̍ vṛ̱ṇakti̍ vi̱ndate̱ vasu̍ ||
translation.text:
12Come now, O Gods, to your celestial station: the Bharadvâjas' priest entreats your favour. He, sacrificing, fain for wealth, hath honoured the Gods vath those who sit and share oblations.
13Agni, drive thou the wicked foe, the evil-hearted thief away, Far, far, Lord of the brave I and give us easy paths.
14Soma, these pressing-stones have called aloud to win thee for our Friend. Destroy the greedy Paṇi, for a wolf is he.
15Ye, O most bountiful, are they who, led by Indra, seek the sky. Give us good paths for travel: guard us well at home.
16Now have we entered on the road that leads to bliss, without a foe, The road whereon a man escapes all enemies and gathers wealth.
